A1.justification: Both PDFs describe REP, and their main text, equations, figures and tables are readable. v1 includes Appendices A–K; v2 ends after its references and points to supplementary material for settings, full results and device evaluation. That material is not supplied, limiting comparison of the earlier appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, accuracy-resource trade-off and ablation results, including additional datasets and Jetson TX2 measurements in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original REP accuracy, forgetting, training-time and memory results, including retained experiments and a new positional layer-dropping study.

M1.justification: The stated prompt-update objective changes from Lclass + λLprompt in v1 Equation (2) to Lclass + Lprompt in v2 Equation (3). This is a limited reported loss change; lightweight query selection, prompt-excluding token merging and feedback-based layer dropping retain their core procedures. Implementation changes or reruns are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions retain disjoint class-incremental learning on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R and PlantDisease. v1 Appendix D additionally evaluates fine-grained classification on Split CUB-200. Its retention cannot be established because v2's referenced supplementary results are unavailable.

E2.justification: Figure 6(i) clearly replaces L2P with DualPrompt in the 4–8GB PlantDisease comparison, although both already appeared elsewhere. However, retention of v1's appendix comparisons against Miro and ADAM variants cannot be checked, leaving the overall comparator change uncertain. OVOR is cited in v2 but is not a demonstrated new baseline evaluation.

E3.justification: Confirmed changes include switching Figure 6(i) from L2P/ViT-L to DualPrompt/ViT-B, adding a protocol that drops 25% of layers at different positions, and extending forgetting evaluation to existing ablation comparisons. However, v2 delegates detailed settings to unavailable supplementary material, preventing comparison of v1's training budgets, batch sizes and other configurations.

E4.justification: v2 adds positional versus random layer-dropping controls in Figure 4 and expands the attention-head profiles in Figure 2. Its 20-task ImageNet-R example already appears in v1 Appendix H, Table 10. Retention of the earlier extended ablations, compute-budget sweeps and hyperparameter sensitivity studies is unresolved, preventing a reliable overall magnitude judgment.

E5.justification: The supplied material retains the same practice of reporting ± values without specifying seeds, repeated-run counts or significance tests. Forgetting uncertainty already appeared in v1's appendix tables. Added forgetting rows and changed uncertainty magnitudes do not establish a new statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Confirmed updates from v1 Table 4 to v2 Table 5 include ImageNet-R accuracies of 59.66 to 61.57 for L2P, 67.45 to 68.13 for DualPrompt, and 75.52 to 75.45 for CODA-Prompt. v2 also adds forgetting results and replaces Figure 6(i)'s resource results under a different method/backbone configuration. Missing supplementary counterparts prevent determining the overall extent of result changes.

T1.justification: v2 Equation (6) changes the ALD threshold equality case to greater-than-or-equal, whereas v1 Algorithm 2 uses a strict greater-than condition. v2 Algorithm 2 still uses the strict condition, creating a formal inconsistency. The remaining scheduling mathematics is largely equivalent, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that lightweight prompt selection, AToM and ALD improve resource efficiency with limited accuracy loss. The ViT-versus-CNN advantage and reported 16–47% training-time and 5–33% memory reductions are retained. The revised title and abstract change emphasis without establishing a different core contribution.

C2.justification: The matched main text adds interpretations of early attention heads and positional versus random layer dropping to motivate ALD. However, v2 Section 3.2.3 identifies Bottom-layer Drop as worst, while Figure 4 shows Top-layer Drop performing worst, making the new interpretation internally inconsistent.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly states α = 0.9 and thresholds of 16 for ViT-L and 12 for ViT-B, clarifying information previously presented through tuning discussion and a inconsistently labelled heatmap. However, v1's optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, iteration-budget and implementation-source details cannot be matched against v2's unavailable supplement.

R1.justification: v2 adds OVOR and Hierarchical Decomposition of Prompt-Based Continual Learning, relating them to methods with or without prompt selection. It also describes compatibility through full or partial integration of REP's components. The principal related-work organization and positioning remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten and condensed. The preliminary empirical study moves from before the method to the experiments section, while algorithm pseudocode and selected earlier appendix material move into the main text. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adopts two-column layout, replaces the illustrated device mapping with Table 1, and combines previously separated memory and accuracy plots in Figure 5. It adds Figure 4, expands attention-head displays, relocates algorithms and restructures tables with forgetting columns. This is substantial visual reorganization beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 makes algorithms more accessible and adds useful forgetting results and layer-dropping controls. However, the new dropping interpretation contradicts Figure 4, and the ALD threshold equation disagrees with its pseudocode. Missing supplementary material also prevents assessing retention of v1's broader validation and reproducibility information, so a reliable net quality judgment is not possible.
